content.text:
In the United States, cancer survival rates vary significantly depending on the type and stage of cancer at diagnosis. The overall 5-year relative survival rate for all cancers combined has improved over the years, reaching a milestone of 70% in recent data. However, this average masks stark differences between cancer types, with some having very high survival rates when detected early and others remaining highly lethal even with modern treatments.

Cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer) - Approximately 12,000 new cases per year
Malignant pleural mesothelioma - Approximately 3,000 new cases per year
Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) - Approximately 4,000 new cases per year
Angiosarcoma - Approximately 2,000 new cases per year
Neuroendocrine tumors (excluding pancreatic NETs) - Approximately 18,000 new cases per year

Lung and bronchus cancer (28%)
Liver cancer (22%)
Ovarian cancer (50%)
Brain cancer (36%)
Colorectal cancer (65%)
